articles.title: Hideo Kojima Says You'll See Him Cameo in a 'Big' Live-Action Movie — But Which One Is It?
articles.summary: Hideo Kojima teased that he's got a cameo in a "big" live-action movie, but he's not saying which one we'll see him in quite yet. The Metal Gear Solid and Death Stranding creator enticed film fans to theorize about his movie career during a surprise installment in the Koji10 podcast.
body: "I already shot a few other things," Kojima said, as translated through YouTube's English captions (via @Genki_JPN ). "Directors and others have asked me to."

The topic came up when reminiscing about his time doing voice acting work as a mole in Zootopia 2. While the Japanese version of the Pixar film had him provide his talents behind the scenes, he suggested this mysterious new project will allow him to be in front of the camera in some capacity.

So as not to spoil the surprise, he said he "can't say" what it is yet, but it is a "big movie." It is indeed live-action, too, but his involvement is so secretive for now that he even refused to tell his hosts where he shot his part.

Kojima is best known for his work as a game developer, but he's also a well-read cinephile, too. Fans routinely turn up for his reviews of movies like Superman, Backrooms, Spider-Man: Brand New Day, and more. Even his social media biography jokes that "70% of my body is made of movies," so it's no surprise to see him continue to be as involved in film as he can manage.

articles.title: Brandon Sanderson's New Sci-Fi Novel Is Included in Amazon's Latest Book Sale
articles.summary: Ahead of Prime Big Deal Days, Amazon has brought back its popular "3 for 2" book sale. A notable inclusion for Brandon Sanderson fans is the sci-fi author's latest book, Blightfall, which marks the start of Riftwake — a new series and the first official expansion to the Cytoverse.
body: Blightfall is less than $2 off on its own, so this sale is only really worth it if you can find two more books you'd want to pair with it. I'd recommend checking out Sanderson's Cosmere universe books, which are also included in the promotion as well.

Brandon Sanderson's Cytoverse is still fairly new. The universe was kicked off by the Skyward series, which focused on building a sci-fi world more grounded in the YA genre. During IGN's interview, Sanderson explained his intention to skew a tad younger with his writing "because the story is about teens who are forced, before their time, into leadership roles on a planet where war has claimed the lives of much of the older population."

Although the Skyward series technically "started" the universe, you don't actually need to read it to jump into Blightfall. Similar to the Cosmere books, this series acts as a new entry point rather than a sequel. That being said, I do highly recommend checking out Skyward as it's actually a terrific original sci-fi fantasy story. Plus there's already a TV series in the works for it.

articles.title: Halloween’s First DLC Reveals Even The Bad Sequels Will Get Some Love
articles.summary: Halloween's first paid DLC is coming on October 27 in the form of a new skin for the game's killer, Michael Myers, and it's pulling from a source you might not expect: Halloween 5: The Revenge of Michael Myers.
body: It may seem odd to jump to the fifth movie for the game's first DLC, but it's not the only piece of new content coming that day. There's also a second skin coming for Big Mike, borrowing from his look in the legacy sequel Halloween (2018). Each skin will run you $10.

Survivor mains also have new things to look forward to, including two new characters, Michelle and Eugene, as well as Civilian Costumes Pack 1, which includes 14 outfits--one for each survivor character--and 42 colorings, or "tints." The new survivors will also go for $10, though that's for the pair, not for each of them, while the new styles and colors will be--you guessed it--$10 for the set. This content drop is the first of several coming to the game in its first year, development studio Illfonic said.

articles.title: Ubisoft Boss Says Watch Dogs Is 'Important' to Company's Future, But Don't Expect Any New Entries Anytime Soon
articles.summary: Don't hold your breath for a new Watch Dogs game anytime soon. As reported by Game File, Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot was asked by an investor about the future of the Watch Dogs franchise.
body: There is a Watch Dogs movie on the horizon, but there's no word on when it will be released. The film wrapped production two years ago and had reshoots last year, but there hasn't been any sort of meaningful promotion for the film to date. As of right now, it doesn't even have a release date, which makes it even more of a mystery.

Watch Dogs made its debut back in 2014, though it was initially meant to launch simultaneously with the PS4 in November 2013. Ubisoft hyped it up as a direct competitor to Grand Theft Auto 5, which released in September 2013. Unfortunately, many felt it was unable to reach some of its ambitions, but it still managed to make a dent in the open-world crime genre. Two years later, Ubisoft launched a much more impressive sequel set in San Francisco, but failed to keep the momentum going with its third installment.
points: Don't hold your breath for a new Watch Dogs game anytime soon.

articles.title: Miami Vice: The Final Director’s Cut’s Ending Invites a Darker Reading of Michael Mann’s Cult Classic
articles.summary: Miami Vice: The Director’s Final Cut’s rejiggered ending invites a slightly darker interpretation of the film than was evident in either of the past versions, especially when considered with what writer-director Michael Mann revealed about the fact-based origins of his screenplay at the…
body: Full SPOILERS follow for all three versions of Michael Mann’s Miami Vice movie.

Mann’s film version of the iconic 1980s TV series, which he executive produced but did not create, has been a love it or hate it affair since it came out in 2006. If you haven’t seen the Unrated Director’s Edition and are only familiar with the theatrical cut, then you will find much to unpack with this Director’s Final Cut when it arrives on 4K UHD and Blu-ray on December 15.

All three versions of Mann’s Miami Vice follow Miami-Dade P.D. undercover detectives James "Sonny" Crockett (a gruff, mustachioed Colin Farrell) and Ricardo Tubbs (a no-nonsense Jamie Foxx), who are recruited to infiltrate a Latin American narco-trafficking network after a mole has been discovered inside a joint Federal task force. Crockett and Tubbs sneak into South America by air and, once there, meet with sinister middleman Jose Yero (a scene-stealing John Ortiz). They succeed in insinuating themselves into Yero and his boss Montoya’s operation.

articles.title: Amid Uncharted 5 Rumors, Nathan Drake Actor Says He Would Come Back, But With One Catch
articles.summary: One of actor Nolan North's most famous roles is that of Nathan Drake in Naughty Dog's Uncharted franchise, but he wrapped things up with 2016's Uncharted 4: A Thief's End.
body: “110%. Absolutely. I think it would be one of the biggest games ever if they decided to do it. It just depends if Sony wants to make money," he said at Gamergy in Puerto Rico prior to the recent rumors of Uncharted 5 ( via DomTheBomb ). "I absolutely would. I try to stay in shape just in case. I can't see a scenario where I would say no. I always keep out hope."
North went on to clarify that he has not heard anything about a new Uncharted game where he might be asked to come back, but he thinks it would be a good business decision for Sony.
"It is a business-my god, can you imagine if they did? It would be the biggest announcement in gaming. I don't think that's hyperbole. I think that's true," he said.
North said he enjoyed working with Naughty Dog over the years on the four main Uncharted games, and that's part of why he would be up to come back.

articles.title: GTA 6 Could Finally Fix Gaming's Huge Drug Problem
articles.summary: People are very excited by recent reports claiming that Grand Theft Auto 6 will allow players to carry cocaine and snort it off their hands at any time. While that’s obviously an entertaining (and thematic) detail, developer Rockstar Games has an opportunity to push the envelope forward in terms of…
body: Rockstar North co-studio head and head of development Aaron Garbut recently told Game Informer, “Normally you compromise scale for detail or detail for interaction, but with this project we went the other way – everything is dialed up, detail, scope, breadth, scale, interaction and density. I don’t think we have ever created anything close to this before.” Elsewhere in Game Informer’s preview, Garbut noted that GTA 6 ’s choice-driven gameplay aims to inspire multiple playthroughs. With all this in mind, I’d be surprised if drug use didn’t have more intricate gameplay consequences than we’ve seen elsewhere.

articles.title: New Gears Of War: E-Day Patch Addresses Giant Vomiting Frog Error Codes
articles.summary: Gears of War: E-Day rolls out worldwide starting October 6, and thanks to early access players, The Coalition has identified several issues that it's fixing with the game's first patch.
body: One of the biggest fixes is the "Bilefrog-Kalona" error, an issue named after the gigantic subterranean Locust frogs encountered throughout the game, which regularly try to kill you by vomiting stomach acid at your position. Nasty stuff. The Coalition assigned several Gears-themed names to its network errors, and in this case, getting vomit-frogged is a specific split-screen multiplayer issue. This triggers when a split-screen player is automatically signed out of online services after the console or PC is suspended, then tries to use Quick Resume to hop back in.

The Coalition says it has also addressed an issue in Versus Social matches that results in players entering a waiting-lobby limbo, and fixed an issue that could prevent certain Siege Blitz Secure objectives from being completed. For the campaign, several pesky problems across Act 2 are being patched, while other game-wide instances of sticky turrets and unearned War Journal progress have been resolved.

articles.title: Why GTA Studio Co-Founder Is Avoiding GTA 6–And All Open-World Games
articles.summary: Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser left the company in 2020 and now runs a new outfit called Absurd Ventures. Houser will be forever connected to the GTA franchise, and he's now weighed in on GTA 6. He told Variety that he did not watch the "Extended Look" trailer and doesn't plan to. Why?
body: "And given that I spend a large amount of time trying to make open-world games, and the rest of my conscious time trying to figure out innovative ways to market them, I don’t need to see what other people are [doing]," he said. "I’m always trying to think about new ways of doing it, not sit there in some kind of comparison of what I would have done differently.”
Also in the interview, Houser said he doesn't play a lot of open-world games anymore, for similar reasons.

"I find when I play them, I can almost deconstruct the strengths and weaknesses of the team in real time and it’s distracting. I’m always thinking, ‘Well, their animation team is weak, but I think this game design is fantastic.’ And, ‘Oh, I can imagine that meeting when they discuss this feature,'" he said. "I’m not a game designer; I’m a sort of creative director. So I’m trying to always find new things that haven’t been done before, or that I can steal from older media, quite frankly or just inspired me or things I always thought about.”

articles.title: 38 Years Ago, 'Doctor Who' Doubled Down on Its Most Inventive Sci-Fi Concept
articles.summary: Across the course of his many lifetimes, the Doctor has faced countless foes, including the Cybermen, the Ice Warriors, and his old schoolmate and frenemy, the Master. Every Whovian has their favorites. Each has tested him, his companions, and even the fate of the universe.
body: However, in 1988, in the waning era before Doctor Who left TV screens for 16 years, a series of episodes had the Doctor fight his greatest enemy for the very last time. Well, before showrunner Russell T. Davies brought them back in the sixth episode of the revival, “Dalek.”

Several seasons and Doctors later, the Doctor returns to Earth with a new face and a new companion, only to discover that two Dalek factions are after the Hand of Omega. They join forces with Captain Gilmore (Simon Williams) and Sergeant Mike Smith (Dursley McLinden), who look to rid Earth of the Dalek threat.

Most Classic Who fans fondly remember “Remembrance of the Daleks.” It’s easy to see why: this is one of the best arcs featuring Seven and Ace. It puts McCoy’s feet to the fire as he portrays a more manipulative Doctor trying to trick the Daleks, and he is perfectly matched by Aldred’s rebellious, tough attitude as Ace.

articles.title: The Zelda: Ocarina of Time Controller's Best Replacement Is $30 Cheaper Right Now
articles.summary: During its September reveal of the first gameplay footage of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, Nintendo also announced a special edition Switch 2 console and Pro Controller. Both the console and the controller have consistently been sold out at all major retailers ever since.
body: Nintendo's website shows an asking price of $74.99 for the Tears of the Kingdom controller. It's currently sold out at Nintendo's online store, though. There has been some confusion online about the price. The Switch 2 Pro Controller currently retails for $89.99, but the Tears of the Kingdom controller is an older, Switch 1 model.

Though they look similar, there are a couple of differences worth noting between the Switch 1 and Switch 2 Pro Controllers. The Switch 2 version, and the Ocarina of Time variant, includes a 3.5mm headphone jack, programmable back buttons (GL/GR), upgraded rumble features, and a dedicated C button for GameChat. If you don't care about any of that stuff, you'll probably be just fine with the older model. The newer Switch 2 version is black, gold and green. Meanwhile, the older one is black, gold, and white. The gold Zonai designs on the older model are more subdued, whereas the newer edition is a bit flashier with its metallic, Triforce-inspired embellishments.

articles.title: GTA 6 devs tried "not to jump on the bandwagon" of passing trends and instead created their "own slanted, overblown versions"
articles.summary: Creating a timely satire can be tough when development takes half a decade or more - it's the reason South Park's stuck with its crude art style for literal decades, but the developers of GTA 6 can't just replace their world-class tech with paper cutouts.
body: "We work on it for years and years," Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, told Love Magazine, "so you need to make content that will feel vital to the moment of release. If there's a trend blowing up for six months, you need to see it for what it is and not jump on the bandwagon." While South Park can centre an entire episode on demonic Labubus and squeeze out some laughs while they're still hot, GTA doesn't quite have the same luxury.

Rather than betting on memes that expired years ago, Rockstar leaned into "things that interested us, like conspiracy theories," Humphries added. "The strange ways the public reacts to everyday occurrences, and those are the kinds of things we ran with. In most cases, rather than trying to put a like-for-like of something real in the world, we have created our own slanted, overblown versions, be that a conspiracy theory, or another universal contemporary phenomenon."

Grand Theft Auto's always been a darkly satirical series, but it frequently tackles tougher subjects too. One notable constant is how the series deals with the American Dream and how the public's attitude toward the American Dream has shifted through the years.

body: According to Deadline, the follow-up to 2018's Sicario: Day of the Soldado will instead be written by Steven Knight, the creator of Peaky Blinders and writer behind films such as Eastern Promises and Spencer.

Last week, Variety reported that original Sicario writer and Yellowstone creator Taylor Sheridan had written the script for the third Sicario film. But according to Deadline, production companies Black Label Media and Thunder Road are going in a different direction, with Knight handling the story.
Padraic McKinley reportedly is on board to direct Sicario 3. McKinley's credits include TV series Fightworld and Kingdom and the recent film The Weight starring Ethan Hawke and Russell Crowe.

articles.title: Steam sale deep cut alert: this ARPG originally developed for Nokia N-Gage is brilliant on Deck
articles.summary: Xanadu Next is a Diablo-esque JRPG originally developed by Nihon Falcom for Nokia N-Gage. Those bullet points were enough for me to grab it when Steam's algorithm surfaced it for me last week as part of the ongoing Autumn sale. I wasn't expecting it to be good, but I was definitely curious.
body: Some background: Xanadu Next is actually a belated spin-off to the PC-88 game Xanadu: Dragon Slayer 2, which was released in 1985 and is sometimes credited as one of the first action RPGs. It took until 2005 for Nihon Falcom to follow it up with Xanadu Next, and when it did it was a Japan only affair.

A PC version did release a few months after the N-Gage version, but again, only in Japan. That PC version reportedly played much, much better than the N-Gage version, as I'm sure you can imagine, but the fact that the game's overarching design was conceived to work across both platforms is what piqued my interest. As did the fact that, when I googled Xanadu Next, I found many people claiming the PC version—which is the version available on Steam—is right up there with the best of Nihon Falcom's games (which is to say, up there with instalments of Ys, Trails and The Legend of Heroes).
points: Xanadu Next is a Diablo-esque JRPG originally developed by Nihon Falcom for Nokia N-Gage.
Those bullet points were enough for me to grab it when Steam's algorithm surfaced it for me last week as part of the ongoing Autumn sale.

articles.title: Halo Studios says "it is absolutely our intent" to release new Halo book, despite layoffs and a rumored lore reboot from Activision
articles.summary: Halo Studios can't promise that the previously-announced Halo novel will land on shop shelves, but the company is "determined" to see the project cross the finish line regardless.
body: Xbox's influential sci-fi series is in the middle of a massive shakeup behind the scenes. As part of the console maker's sweeping restructure, mass layoffs hit developer Halo Studios and the entire series moved under Activision's supervision. Xbox's Matt Booty said "a small team at Halo Studios will continue supporting the Halo community and games in-market."
Now, franchise writer Alex Wakeford has addressed what's happening with two of the series' upcoming stories - Troy Denning's Halo: Fireteam Noble and Kenneth Peters' Halo: Burn the Road Home novella.

"Many have been asking whether this novel will still be releasing," Wakeford wrote in a recent Halo Waypoint blog post, speaking about Fireteam Noble. "To this we can say that it is absolutely our intent to see this project cross the finish line. Troy has written a fantastic story and a good chunk of the editorial process has been conducted. In my remaining time at the studio, I will be doing all I can to ensure this can be achieved."
As for the newly-revealed novella, Wakeford also said "we are determined to see this through to completion."
points: Halo Studios can't promise that the previously-announced Halo novel will land on shop shelves, but the company is "determined" to see the project cross the finish line regardless.

videos.summary: Something truly wicked is being unleashed during Season 5: A Grim Doctrine.
body: The wait is over! Our newest Support Hero is here with the arrival of Doctrine. Freed from his volcanic prison by Doomfist himself, this sinister foe can manipulate life using his Eternal Scepter and mechanical drones, while also empowering each ability with his signature Infuse.

Break into Watchpoint: Grímsvötn - the Icelandic prison that once held Doctrine and Doomfist, and our first new Escort Map since Overwatch 2 launched. Battle your way through fire and ice as the final chapter in the Reign of Talon starts right here.

The Halloween mayhem continues this year with our newest event, Mystery Madness: Graveyard Games. You’ll start off as a random Hero and unlock random new powers each time you die. Complete chilling challenges to collect Offerings and help summon the next Hero into the madness.

videos.title: DuneCrawl - Release Trailer | PS5 Games
videos.summary: DuneCarwl is coming to PS5 on October 19th, 2026 with Cross-Play Support.
body: DuneCrawl is an open world action-adventure game, where you take to the sandy seas atop a gigantic crustacean festooned with black powder cannons. Play as a solo Crab Keeper, or with a crew of up to three other friends in local and online coop.
